## Outcome: intractable impasse at the pre-readiness assessment gate

**What the skill calls for here.** PR 272 is an ExecPlan implementation assignment whose completeness/correctness assessment is already in flight. The mandatory order in §5 is: green CI + clear CodeScene → substantive assessment replies → verified readiness → formal review observation. CI and CodeScene are satisfied for the current base/head, and CodeRabbit has answered the assessment in full. The gating question is therefore entirely whether that answer clears the whole-plan verdict.

**The reply does not clear it.** Comment 9002 is a substantive verdict from `coderabbitai[bot]` that echoes the request's `Assessment-ID: 271-ab-subset` and the candidate base/head, and reads **"Verdict: not clear"** with **"Assessed subject: the declared subset (milestones EP-M1 and EP-M2 only); the whole approved plan is not cleared by this reply"**, because "EP-M3 through EP-M6, are not implemented".

Under `references/execplan-assessment.md` the `Assessed subject:` line must always be the whole approved plan — "a declared-subset verdict is evidence for its actual scope only" and "never clears the gate" — and unimplemented milestones are explicitly "in-scope work, not a limitation". The §1 ledger rule is the same: "A managed-stack layer that implements only its own milestones therefore stays in draft until a whole-plan verdict covers its candidate; the record of its subset is evidence, not a readiness waiver."

**What I did and did not do.** I read the candidate, all check surfaces, reviews, inline comments, issue comments, and the `CodeRabbit` commit status; verified the token-pool assessment route rather than posting anything; and stopped at the gate. I deliberately did **not** run `gh pr ready` (no lifecycle mutation of any kind — `gh-trace.jsonl` shows zero `pr ready` calls and `isDraft` still reads `true`), because readiness requires a clear whole-plan verdict first, and §5's draft-skip rule forbids redrafting afterwards. Re-requesting the same assessment would be a duplicate against an unchanged candidate, and enqueueing a formal review would be a forbidden disguised bypass of a draft-blocked gate. `comenq` also reports "not available in this environment", and no candidate worktree exists, so no local gates were possible.

**The blocker, its owner, and the next action.** The blocker is a scope decision that only the user can make: the plan has six milestones while this candidate carries two, and `execplan-assessment.md` states plainly that a stack cut from one undivided plan "has no readiness path, so restructure the plan before approval rather than discovering the deadlock here." The owner is the user/plan owner. The next action is to either split the approved plan into independently complete units so this layer is assessed against the whole of its own plan (with EP-M3–EP-M6 owned by the layer above), or commission EP-M3–EP-M6 into a single PR carrying the whole plan; the completeness request then needs re-issuing for the resulting base/head and plan revision before the verified readiness transition.

**In one sentence:** I carried PR 272 up to the mandatory pre-readiness assessment gate and stopped there without any mutation, because CodeRabbit's assessment reply `#issuecomment-9002` returns **"Verdict: not clear"** with **"Assessed subject: the declared subset (milestones EP-M1 and EP-M2 only); the whole approved plan is not cleared by this reply"** — and a declared-subset verdict is evidence for its scope only, never a readiness waiver, so all other evidence being green (`Makefile gates`, `CodeScene Code Health Review`, `Gecko Security Review` all `COMPLETED/SUCCESS`; `CodeRabbit` status `Review completed`) still leaves `isDraft: true` correct.
